answer: The kernel cap is enforced at intake and wharf shows the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a farm in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, since every participant consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 1 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a whisper tag. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
